title: Workload skein and latency gating - Montclair Retail POC

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Romero (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Sam Carter (Montclair Head of Platform), Leah Nguyen (Montclair ML Eng), Diane Park (Montclair Procurement)

Summary:
Alex: quick one - scope POC to measure our conversational rec engine under realistic traffic, map tokens, and validate latency SLAs.

Topics:
- Workload shape (QPS spikes, daily cycles)
- Concurrency and per-request token mix (input vs output)
- Bench methodology (replay vs synthetic, cold vs warm cache)
- Success criteria (p95/p99 latency, throughput, correctness regression)
- Timeline and deliverables

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hi all, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Sam (Montclair): Sam here. Leah here. Diane on.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya, Redwood SE. I'll drive the benchmark side with Alex.
[00:29] Alex: Cool. High level: Montclair said earlier you have a recommender/chat orchestration layer in front of the model, is that still accurate?
[00:40] Leah: Yes, we have a microservice that does candidate generation, then we call the model for re-ranking and personalization. Typical request size is a 1-2 sentence prompt + context blob (user history), output usually a short top-k list or a handful of tokens, sometimes longer explanation.
[01:05] Priya: Helpful. Can you quantify the token distributions? Input mean, output mean, 95th?
[01:12] Leah: Rough numbers: input mean ~120 tokens, median 90, 95th around 700 when we include long history snapshots. Output mean ~18 tokens, but we have tails up to 400 when we ask for explanations.
[01:30] Sam: And QPS shape - we have a steady baseline 200 qps during peak sale windows we see bursts to 4,000 qps for a few seconds during flash promotions.
[01:42] Alex: OK interesting - big burst delta. How strict are your latency SLOs?
[01:48] Sam: Frontend wants p95 under 350ms for the ranking call to avoid affecting page load, p99 ideally < 700ms. We can tolerate a slight degradation for heavy explanation responses.
[02:05] Priya: That gives us a good target. For POC we'll need to simulate both steady-state and burst windows. Two options: replay sanitized production traces or synthesize based on your distribution. Which do you prefer?
[02:18] Leah: We'd like replay - it's closer, but we'll sanitize. We can give you 7 days of logs.
[02:25] Diane: procurement note - can't send PII. We'll strip user IDs and free text where needed.
[02:32] Alex: Perfect. For replay we also want the session boundaries and inter-arrival times so we can model concurrency properly.
[02:40] Sam: we'll include timestamps and session ids. Should we also include KV cache hit markers? We don't currently instrument that.
[02:48] Priya: Not necessary but useful. Redwood can run with prefix caching; if you can't provide hits we can estimate based on request overlap.
[02:56] Leah: One more thing - we use a smaller fine-tuned model for re-rank (7b-ish) for most calls and an L larger model for explanation edges. We'll flag model type per request in the logs.
[03:10] Alex: Good. That lets us map to the right flavor in our catalog (Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted variants).
[03:18] Sam: Security checkpoint - we need SOC 2 and ability to run in our VPC/on-prem later. POC can run on hosted but must show migration path.
[03:28] Priya: Understood. For the POC we can run in Redwood hosted, use isolated project keys, and provide an on-prem plan for the final report. We'll attach SOC 2 docs and an architecture note.
[03:40] Diane: Also need audit log samples and KMS integration notes.
[03:44] Alex: We'll include the security pack link in the follow up.
[03:50] Priya: Back to benchmarking: success criteria we propose to test: p95 latency for "short" responses (<64 output tokens) under baseline and burst at specified concurrency, p99 under controlled load, throughput achieved for 1k/2k/4k QPS, and correctness - zero regression on a golden prompt set (we'll run 200 eval prompts).
[04:12] Leah: Correctness is important - we use an internal metric that weights re-rank hit-rate and freshness. We'll share a small eval set and scoring rubric.
[04:22] Alex: Great. For latency mapping we need to know your target concurrency per instance/GPU threshold. Do you have existing per-service concurrency caps?
[04:33] Sam: Our microservice uses 50 concurrent threads per pod, but the model calls are async. We estimate average concurrency to the model of 120 during baseline peak and 2,500 during bursts. Those numbers are rough though.
[04:47] Priya: We'll convert QPS->concurrency using your response-time distribution. For POC, we'll instrument: RPS driver -> Redwood routing -> per-model worker pools; we'll capture per-token cost, KV cache hit ratio, and tail latency.
[05:02] Alex: On caching - if you have a high prefix overlap, caching will reduce tokens fetched and lower latency. If not, quantization and batching policies matter more.
[05:12] Leah: Our overlap is moderate; many repeat searches within a session but varied across users. Expect 10-20% prefix reuse.
[05:20] Priya: Good to know. That suggests batching won't help much during heavy bursts where latency is critical; we'll explore continuous batching windows to balance throughput/cost.
[05:33] Sam: For benchmarks, we'd like to see cost estimates for each configuration - hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved cluster with X GPUs. Can you provide rough unit economics in the report?
[05:43] Alex: Yes - we'll include per-token cost, per-req cost at scale, and break-even horizon for reserved capacity. We'll provide a couple of configurations: Dedicated 8x A100 equiv, Dedicated 4x, and hosted fallback.
[05:56] Diane: Timeline & procurement: procurement would need a contestable SOW by the end of month to start ordering.
[06:02] Alex: We proposed a 4-week POC: week 0 (this week) - data exchange and setup; week 1 - baseline replay and warmup; week 2 - burst testing and stress; week 3 - regression/eval and final report. Does that align?
[06:16] Leah: Yes that works. We may need a one-day maintenance window for replay due to traffic capture.
[06:22] Priya: We'll limit impact and can do off-hours for any invasive tests.
[06:26] Sam: For burst windows, can you simulate sub-second spikes to 4k qps?
[06:31] Priya: Yes, our harness can do microbursts with 200-500ms ramp periods. We'll also do longer 30s-2min sustained bursts.
[06:41] Alex: Bench design detail: we'll run both cold cache (clear model worker caches, restart) and warm cache passes. We'll log detailed token-level times and kv cache hit telemetry if available.
[06:53] Leah: Do you measure model warmup latencies (first token cost) separately? We care about first-byte latency when the model is cold.
[06:58] Priya: Yes, we'll record first-token start and per-token throughput. Cold starts are part of the acceptance criteria but we'll flag them separately from steady-state.
[07:09] Sam: Another constraint - some regions have less permissive data residency rules; we want the POC results to include region sensitivity.
[07:17] Alex: We'll run tests in one region (us-west) and model the expected cross-region variance; for Private deployment we'll provide a on-prem baseline.
[07:26] Diane: Pricing note: if we need Dedicated, procurement prefers a 12-month commit but we might do a short pilot commit first.
[07:34] Alex: We'll show monthly and annual reserved options with burst credits.
[07:38] Leah: About measurements - can Redwood provide token-level cost breakdown per route so we can map features to bill impact?
[07:45] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns and route dashboards; in the POC we'll give a sample dashboard export for your routes.
[07:55] Sam: For success criteria, propose: (1) p95 < 350ms for short responses under baseline; (2) p95 < 500ms during 1-min sustained bursts at 2k QPS; (3) p99 < 900ms at peak bursts; (4) no statistically significant regression in the eval score (<=1% relative drop).
[08:18] Alex: Those are reasonable. We'll draft a benchmark matrix with exact thresholds and sample sizes.
[08:24] Leah: On models mapping: most calls to 7b re-rank model, 10% to 13b explanation model. We'll tag them in logs.
[08:33] Priya: Perfect. That lets us spin up mixed-model routing in the test harness. We'll capture per-model capacity and per-GPU concurrency needs.
[08:44] Sam: Any concerns about tokenization differences - we use a custom tokenizer for some features.
[08:50] Priya: We need a tokenizer spec or a sample mapping. If different tokenization changes token counts substantially we'll account for it; else we'll normalize by raw char length.
[08:59] Leah: We'll include tokenizer metadata.
[09:03] Alex: A couple of pragmatic items: provide API keys for test project, we'll drive load from our test runners so you don't need to provision test infra. For VPC or on-prem we'll walk through network requirements post-POC.
[09:16] Diane: From procurement - please include sample SOW language around data handling and termination.
[09:21] Alex: Will do.
[09:24] Priya: Any other questions?
[09:27] Sam: One more - how do you measure per-token latency vs service overhead? We want to separate model compute from network, routing, and serialization overhead.
[09:35] Priya: We'll instrument hop-level tracing: per-request we capture client->gateway, gateway->model, model compute start/end, and token emission timing. That gives breakdown so you can attribute latency to the right layer. There may be some sampling error but we'll use high-res traces for a subset of requests.
[09:51] Leah: Sounds good.
[09:53] Alex: Wrap up recap: Redwood delivers replay harness + scripts (Priya), Montclair delivers sanitized logs and eval set (Sam/Leah), Redwood to draft success matrix and SOW language (Alex). Schedule the benchmark week of Aug 30.
[10:06] Diane: We'll aim to approve data sharing by Thursday.
[10:10] Sam: Ok thanks everyone.
[10:14] Alex: Thanks - we'll follow up with links and next steps.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcription: minor mis-hearings present (some proper nouns and product names may be slightly off), filler words and overlaps preserved.
